BiblicalUsage: A shoot is a branch, and Isaiah's shoot is the Messiah: a rod out of the stem of Jesse, a Branch growing out of his roots. The same word names the cast-out branch of the king of Babylon, the branch of God's planting in the restored people, and the branch of a queen's roots that rises to take a throne.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Branch is the thread through the book: every shoot that is not His is cut down, and the one shoot from Jesse grows into the kingdom. Isaiah's Branch grows out of Jesse's roots, and the cast-out branch of Babylon is thrown on the stones — the same word, two opposite trees.
